methods.steps: Take a full-page screenshot, choose File > Import in Inkscape and pick it; a dialog asks whether to link or embed the image, and embedding stores it inside the SVG file.
methods.limits: The SVG holds a picture, not editable text.

methods.steps: The library lists domToSvg among its functions; it runs inside a web page you control.
methods.limits: A developer route; the README gives no domToSvg example.
Only extracts existing SVG, not the whole HTML page; fonts and styles must be resolved.

methods.steps: Open the ICO, choose File > Export As (Shift+Ctrl+E) and export it as SVG; in the Export Image as SVG dialog, Embed raster layers as PNG (always) includes raster layers as PNG images.
methods.limits: The SVG holds the picture. The Export As menu path and shortcut are on https://docs.gimp.org/3.0/en/gimp-file-export-as.html; GIMP opening ICO comes from the format reference.

methods.steps: Run magick favicon.ico favicon.png, following the magick image.jpg image.png example; the formats table lists ICO as readable.
methods.limits: Saves a PNG, not an SVG.

methods.steps: File > Import a PNG, select it, Path > Trace Bitmap, Update for the preview, confirm with OK.
methods.limits: Not a 100% faithful vector copy; suits dark silhouettes on a bright background; color tracing makes one object per color.

methods.steps: Open the file (GIMP imports it as a new project in XCF), choose File > Export As (Shift+Ctrl+E), which stores the image in a format other than XCF, and export it as PNG.
methods.limits: JIF as input comes from the format reference (GIMP listed as opening JIF); the menu path and shortcut are on https://docs.gimp.org/3.0/en/gimp-file-export-as.html.

methods.steps: Open the JPG, choose File > Export As (Shift+Ctrl+E) and export as TGA; the Export Image as TarGA dialog has a Use RLE compression checkbox and an Origin choice of Bottom left or Top left.
methods.limits: Origin only affects how the data is stored. The Export As menu path is on https://docs.gimp.org/3.0/en/gimp-file-export-as.html; opening a JPG as a new project is on https://docs.gimp.org/3.0/en/gimp-images-out.html.

methods.steps: Run magick fabric-reference.jpg fabric-texture.tga (the magick input output pattern); the format table lists Truevision Targa as readable and writable.
methods.limits: Tested locally: a JPG converts to TGA with this command.

methods.steps: ffmpeg -i personal-tone.m4r -vn -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k personal-alert.mp3; libmp3lame is the LAME wrapper and b sets the bitrate in bits/s for CBR or ABR.
methods.limits: The codecs page does not name M4R; the command was run locally on an M4R and exited 0.
Needs an FFmpeg build with libx264; the settings differ from this page's.
Page documents libvpx-vp9, crf and libopus; run locally, exit 0.
Composed documented flags; requires valid audio stream and decoder.
ffmpeg.html documents -i, -b:v and guessing the output format from the extension; run locally with a .mov, exit 0; sets only the video bitrate.
ffmpeg.html documents -vn, -c:a, -b:a and guessing the format from the extension; libopus is listed in ffmpeg-codecs.html; run locally on an MP3 with cover art, exit 0.
